title: How to look at a painting
examples: What is the difference between describing and interpreting a painting?
When should I use art vocabulary in my writing?
Can I judge a painting if I do not like it?

explain.say: First we learn to describe what we see in the painting.

draw.text: How to look at a painting

explain.say: Next we analyse by looking at how the artist used their tools.

items: Step 1: Look at light and shadow

explain.say: Then we interpret to suggest what the artwork might mean.
After that we judge by giving your thoughtful opinion on its success.
In real life you see this when looking at a photograph.
A common mistake is confusing description with interpretation.

draw.text: Don't just say what it is

faq.q: How do I know when to stop describing and start analysing?
faq.a: You move from describing what you see to analysing how the artist made it. You should start analysing when you notice specific techniques like colour or line. You could also ask, 'How did the artist create this effect?'
asks: What is the difference between describing and analysing?

faq.q: Is it okay to interpret a painting in a way the artist never intended?
faq.a: Yes, interpretation is your educated guess about meaning. Art history allows for many valid readings of a single piece. You should always support your interpretation with evidence from the painting itself. You might also ask, 'What could this mean?'
asks: Can I be wrong about the meaning?
How do I support my interpretation?

faq.q: Does judging mean I have to say if it is 'good' or 'bad'?
faq.a: No, judging means giving a reasoned opinion based on criteria. You should explain why you feel a certain way using evidence. For example, you could say, 'The composition is weak because...' You could also ask, 'What makes art successful?'
asks: Is judging the same as liking it?
How do I give an opinion without just saying 'I like it'?

faq.q: Do I need to use art vocabulary for all four steps?
faq.a: It is helpful to use specific vocabulary in all stages. Using terms like 'chiaroscuro' or 'composition' shows your understanding. You can also ask, 'What art words should I use?'

faq.q: What is the best order to use these four skills?
faq.a: The standard and safest order is describe, then analyse, then interpret, and finally judge. This builds your argument logically. You could also ask, 'Can I mix up the order?'

facts: Description involves naming elements like colour, shape, and line.
Analysis looks at the artist's techniques, such as perspective or texture.
Interpretation suggests possible meanings based on context or emotion.
Judging requires supporting your opinion with specific visual evidence.

quiz.say: A student writes: 'The bright red colour makes the painting feel angry.' Which skill are they using?
quiz.why: This answer suggests a feeling or meaning, which is the job of interpretation.

wrong.0: Describing only names what is physically there, like 'red colour'.
wrong.1: Analysing looks at how the colour was applied, not what it means.
wrong.2: Judging is giving a final verdict on the work's quality.

quiz.say: Which statement is purely factual observation?

options.show: The figures are painted with soft edges.
options.say: The figures are painted with soft edges.

options.show: There are three figures standing by a river.
options.say: There are three figures standing by a river.

quiz.why: This statement only names things and counts them without suggesting meaning or technique.

wrong.0: This suggests a meaning, which is interpretation.
wrong.1: This is an analysis of technique, not just a count.
wrong.2: This is a judgment of quality.
